articles.title: Kerala Legislators Set for Salary Increase and iPad Purchases Amid Budget Concerns
articles.description: The Kerala government is considering a significant salary increase of 43% for its legislators while also planning to purchase 480 Apple iPads for ministers and their staff. This decision has sparked debates about government spending, especially as it coincides with calls for budget cuts. The procurement process for the iPads has already begun, with an estimated cost of ₹6.71 crores. As discussions unfold, the final details regarding the salary increase and the implications of these purchases on public finances remain to be seen. The situation raises important questions about the necessity of such expenditures in the current economic climate.

articles.title: PIB Fact Check debunks viral claims of new Rs 1,000 note, says RBI has made no announcement
articles.description: New Delhi, Oct 27 (IANS) The Press Information Bureau's (PIB) Fact Check unit on Tuesday dismissed as fake a series of viral social media claims suggesting that a new Rs 1,000 currency note has been issued or is set to be introduced in India. The clarification came after several posts circulated across platforms such as Instagram, X and Telegram, showing individuals holding a purported yellow-coloured Rs 1,000 note. Some social media users and content creators claimed that the currency note was newly introduced or would be launched on a specific date. Rejecting the claims, PIB Fact Check said that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has made no announcement regarding the issuance of a new Rs 1,000 banknote. Custom Ad: Multiplex In a post on X, the government agency urged citizens to verify information only through official sources and refrain from sharing unverified content online. "Several social media posts claim that a new Rs 1,000 note has been issued. This claim is fake," it said. "The RBI has made no announcement regarding the issuance of a new Rs 1,000 note," PIB Fact Check added. The clarification seeks to curb misinformation surrounding the viral images of the purported banknote, which sparked speculation among social media users. Authorities have advised people to exercise caution while consuming and sharing such content and to report suspicious claims to PIB Fact Check. At present, India has banknotes in active circulation in denominations of Rs 10, Rs 20, Rs 50, Rs 100, Rs 200 and Rs 500 under the RBI's Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series. The original Rs 1,000 note ceased to be legal tender on November 8, 2016, when the government announced the demonetisation of existing Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 currency notes as part of efforts to curb black money, counterfeit currency and corruption. While a redesigned Rs 500 note was subsequently introduced, the Rs 1,000 denomination was not brought back into circulation. Instead, the RBI introduced a Rs 2,000 note, which was later withdrawn from circulation in May 2023. --IANS pk

articles.title: Kerala’s Fiscal Crisis: MLA Salary Hike to ₹1 Lakh, 480 iPads in Tender | Sunny Joseph | News18
articles.description: Kerala’s proposed MLA salary hike and a tender to purchase 480 iPads have sparked a debate over government spending amid the state’s fiscal crisis. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Sunny Joseph has said discussions on revising the salaries and allowances of MLAs and ministers are nearing a final decision. He cited rising petrol prices, inflation and increasing day-to-day expenses as reasons for the proposed revision. An MLA currently receives around ₹70,000 per month in salary and allowances, with the proposal seeking to raise the amount to ₹1 lakh. The government has also issued a tender for 480 iPads, reportedly intended for legislators, ministers and their personal staff. The proposals raise questions about fiscal priorities, public expenditure and the need for austerity amid financial pressures. Is the proposed salary hike justified by rising living costs, or should the government prioritise financial discipline? Watch the latest Kerala political news, the MLA salary revision proposal, the iPad procurement controversy and the debate over public spending. n18oc_breaking-news

articles.title: GeM Launches AABHAR Collection to Promote India's Regional Craft Hubs
articles.description: GeM has launched The AABHAR Collection, an online portal showcasing regional handicrafts and GI-tagged goods to boost local artisans and integrate indigenous craft heritage into the national public procurement and institutional gifting landscape.
